summary:
Left Behind is an educational interactive experience designed to introduce children aged 10–14 to the human-made equipment and vehicles left on the Moon and Mars after space missions. Although NASA provides extensive information about these objects, the information is distributed across different sources, making it difficult for young audiences to explore and connect their stories in one accessible place.
Our project addresses this gap by bringing these stories together through an engaging website that combines simplified scientific and historical information, interactive 3D models, visual storytelling, and an educational game. Through this experience, we aim to make space exploration history more accessible, enjoyable, and meaningful for younger generations.
details:
Left Behind is an interactive educational website designed to introduce children aged 10–14 to the human-made equipment, tools, and vehicles left behind on the Moon and Mars after space missions.

The experience begins with an interactive timeline that allows users to select a specific date and discover which piece of equipment is associated with that point in space exploration history. Users can then choose between the Moon and Mars to explore the objects left on each planet.

Each object is presented through an interactive 3D model accompanied by a simplified summary of its historical and scientific information, making it easier for young users to understand what it is, why it was sent, and its role in space missions.

At the end of the website, users are invited to continue their journey through an introductory video featuring a child character who encourages them to explore the equipment. The experience also includes an educational game called LOST SIGNAL. In the game, players receive a hint about a specific piece of equipment and must guess which of three hidden locations contains it. Once they find the correct location, its 3D model and related information are revealed.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

The project brings information about space objects left on the Moon and Mars together in one accessible and engaging experience. Although extensive information about these objects is available through NASA, it is distributed across different sources. Left Behind makes these stories easier for children to discover, understand, and connect with.

Our goal is to encourage curiosity about space exploration, introduce younger generations to its history, and turn learning scientific information into an enjoyable experience rather than simply reading facts.

Creativity and Design Considerations:

The creative aspect of the project lies in combining historical information, interactive 3D models, a timeline, and a guessing game within one child-friendly educational experience. Instead of presenting the information as a traditional collection of articles, users explore it through visual interaction and playful discovery.

During the design process, we considered the target age group (10–14), the need to simplify scientific information without losing its meaning, ease of navigation, and making the experience visually engaging and accessible for children.

Tools and Technologies:

As an industrial design-focused team without a dedicated software developer, we used Figma Websites and Figma Make to design and build the website experience and its interactive features, rather than developing it from scratch through traditional coding.

For the introductory video, we used Google Flow for AI-assisted video generation and CapCut for editing and post-production.
